title: Is Ciena's Pricing Power Real, Or Just A Parts Shortage?
summary: Ciena (CIEN) trades near $334, a little over half its 52-week high, and the easy read on an AI networking supplier down that far is that it has gone on sale. It is still up more than 150% over the past year, and the company has just guided fiscal 2027 to record profitability. The risk here is not demand. It is what the new prices are attached to.

title: Jim Cramer Says the AI Slowdown Is Fake. Dell Is His Evidence.
summary: Jim Cramer built his case that AI spending fears are overblown on three stocks, but two of them moved in the exact wrong direction on the day he made the call.

title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For The Cash As Apple Leaves?
summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) throws off free cash worth 5.2% of its market value each year, against 4.4% for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median means one of two things: a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Here it is mostly the second: the cash comes from smartphone chips, and Apple is leaving.

title: How Far Can NVIDIA Stock Fall In A Demand Scare?
summary: NVIDIA (NVDA) stock trades near $212, about 10% below its 52-week high, and it has gone nowhere over the past three months. The company itself has not been standing still. So it is worth asking the uncomfortable question: how far does a stock like this fall when a real shock arrives, and how long would you wait to get it back.

title: OpenAI’s CFO Just Explained Why Nvidia Is No Longer the Only Option
summary: OpenAI's CFO just revealed how $122 billion in cash fundamentally changes the power dynamic between the world's most important AI lab and its chip suppliers, and the implications for Nvidia's premium pricing are only beginning to surface.

OpenAI's CEO echoed similar caution, which prompted investors to reassess longer term demand assumptions for AI chips and infrastructure suppliers. title: This AI Stock Could Be Worth Far More Than Investors Think
summary: Broadcom just posted AI revenue growth of 221% year over year and guided for even bigger numbers ahead, yet the stock sits well off its highs and trades at a fraction of its closest custom-chip rival's multiple. Something in that math does not add up.
